2	
3	Framework: Aura3D (`@aura3d/engine`, already installed in node_modules; three.js 0.185.1 is also installed for procedural asset factories, see BRIDGE.md).
4	
5	Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, drawing into the existing canvas with id #app. Show a studio product shot of three spheres of equal size in a row on a seamless, softly lit, light-grey floor that curves up into the backdrop. Left sphere: clear glass (transparent, with refraction or at least a convincing tint, bright specular highlights and visible reflections of the studio lights). Centre sphere: brushed metal such as steel or aluminium (strongly metallic, with a stretched or blurred reflection that is clearly different from the glass). Right sphere: woven fabric such as dark red velvet or wool (fully rough, no mirror reflections, soft sheen or fuzzy rim light, a fine procedural weave or noise pattern visible up close). Light the scene like a photography studio: one large soft key light, a dimmer fill from the opposite side and a rim light from behind, plus an environment or reflection source so the metal and glass have something to reflect. The spheres cast soft contact shadows on the floor. The camera is fixed at a slightly raised, three-quarter-front angle with all three spheres fully in frame and centred. 1	# three.js asset bridge (`aura3d import-three`)
2	
3	Carry procedural three.js content into an Aura3D project as a typed asset plus editable Aura3D source, instead of
4	porting it by hand. The bridge carries assets, animation clips, simple shaders, lights, camera and renderer output.
5	Behaviour (input, physics, scoring, UI) stays native Aura3D code. It is a build-time tool: `three` is a dev
6	dependency of your project, never a runtime dependency, and the shipped route imports only `@aura3d/engine`.
7	
8	Status: prototype (B1). Every run writes a report of what was carried, approximated or left out; read it before
9	you show the result.
10	
11	## When to use it
12	
13	| You have | Use |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| A three.js function that builds a scene from code (procedural props, a generated city, an animated rig, a shader showcase) | `aura3d import-three` |

17	| A GLB file | `aura3d assets add` |
